important.name: This repo flips to the project profile on release, and nothing tracks the fix
important.summary:
The new default is `strap.target: project`, and this repo's `.claude/harness.json` does not set `harness`. The design states it does (line 83). The plan (TASK-1) defers the line because the published 0.50.0 schema would reject the key. That is a fair reason, but no TODO or plan item tracks the follow-up. Once 0.51.0 is published, `strap.py new <name>` in operator-straps opens a project-profile spec and scaffolds into `.claude/skills/<name>/` instead of `plugins/harness/skills/<name>/`. The only kind of skill this repo straps then goes to the wrong place.

Also (docs): docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-03-strap-skills-target-aware-design.md:83 states that this repo's `.claude/harness.json` sets `"strap": {"target": "harness"}`. At head `.claude/harness.json` has no `strap` key, so `new_fields` (plugins/harness/lib/harness_lib/strap_profile.py:110-113) falls through to the project profile. The plan records this as deferred (0003 ActionPlan `deferred_to_future_plans`), but nothing a session reads before running `strap.py new` says so. A new harness skill strapped in this repo with the local plugin (the `--plugin-dir` route CLAUDE.md recommends, and the one the pending STR-11 session uses) would land under `.claude/skills/<name>/` instead of `plugins/harness/skills/<name>/`. Open specs are not affected because the recorded `plugin_dir` pins them.

Also (system_shape): design.md:83 states 'This repo's .claude/harness.json sets "strap": {"target": "harness"}'. At the PR head, .claude/harness.json has no strap key, and the plan defers the line (ActionPlan deferred_to_future_plans, PIP TASK-1) because the published 0.50.0 schema would reject it. The deferral is reasoned. The effect: after merge, until a follow-up lands, `strap.py new <name>` in this repo opens a project-profile spec under .claude/skills/ instead of plugins/harness/skills/. Nothing in the README or the strap-skills SKILL.md warns about this, and the only tracker is the plan's deferred list.
fix: Add a docs/TODO item (or a plan follow-up) to set `"strap": {"target": "harness"}` in `.claude/harness.json` once 0.51.0 is published, and change design line 83 to say the line is deferred until that release.
Have `strap.py new` warn when the project profile is chosen in a repository whose plugin manifest is named `harness`, so the deferred config cannot fail silently.

Leave the frozen spec as it is. Add a short note to CLAUDE.md (Rules for changes) saying that until a release carries the `strap` schema key, `strap.py new` here opens project-profile specs, and that a new harness skill must wait for the `strap.target: harness` line in `.claude/harness.json`.
Open a tracked TODO or issue for the deferred `.claude/harness.json` edit, gated on the 0.51.0 release, and cite it from the plan's deferred entry.
Track the follow-up (set strap.target to harness in .claude/harness.json once 0.51.0 is published) as an item in the docs/TODO catalog, so it lands right after the merge.
Since the design spec is frozen, record the divergence from design.md:83 in the plan's deferred entry text, which already exists, rather than editing the spec.

important.name: Prose-only project SKILL.md tells the author to rerun scaffold, which refuses a new spec
important.summary: _NO_API_SECTION (rendered into a project SKILL.md when no API part is planned) says 'Add a mechanical behavior and rerun scaffold, or delete this section.' For a NEW spec, render_parts (strap_scaffold.py:174-178) raises StrapError as soon as any planned target exists ('<name> is a new skill but these parts exist: ...'), and the SKILL.md just rendered is always one of them. Even if the refusal were lifted, an existing SKILL.md is never re-rendered (line 181 renders only missing targets), so the API section would still not appear. The only guidance the generated file gives for adding an API later leads to a refusal.
fix: Reword _NO_API_SECTION to a path that works, e.g. 'TODO(fill): this skill has no API module yet. To add one, add a mechanical behavior, list the models and API modules with add_part, and copy the heredoc from the strap-skills project api_section template; or delete this section.'

Let render_parts for a NEW spec write the missing parts when every existing target is a scaffold-owned part already listed in spec.parts, and document that the SKILL.md API section must then be added by hand.

important.name: Contract-test load idiom gives the API a second copy of the models classes
important.summary: The scaffolded `_load` registers each module as `<stem>_under_contract`, but the rendered API does a bare sibling import (`from <snake>_models import ...`), so loading both yields two distinct `Entry`/`Document` classes. SKILL.md step 2 tells authors to copy this idiom into planned tests. A planned test that builds `models.Entry(...)` and hands it to `api.add_entry` fails the `isinstance(entry, Entry)` check (api.tmpl:105) with `add_entry takes an Entry built by new_entry`. The test is correct, and the error points at the wrong cause. The shipped contract test avoids the trap only because no test there crosses the two modules.
fix: In contract_test.tmpl `_load`, register under the bare stem (`spec_from_file_location(stem, path)`, `sys.modules[stem] = module`) and return `sys.modules[stem]` when it is already loaded, so the API's sibling import and the test share one models module; update the step 2 prose in strap-skills SKILL.md to state that the module is registered under its own stem.
Keep the alias, and have SKILL.md step 2 tell planned tests to take models classes from the API's namespace (`sys.modules['<snake>_models']`) rather than from a separately loaded copy.

minor.name: Plan 0003 evidence cites a commit that is not in the PR history
minor.summary:
Every COMPLETE item in docs/plans/0003_strap_skills_target_aware_ActionPlan.json (lines 23-27, 82-86, ... 616-619) and its rendered PIP records `commit 156cbf1` / `tree 2300ac65...` as its evidence. 156cbf1 exists locally but is not an ancestor of the head dd2089c (`git merge-base --is-ancestor` exits 1), and its tree matches none of the PR's commits: the work was apparently re-split into 544b290..dd2089c after `plan.py record` ran. Once the branch is merged and that local commit is pruned, the recorded evidence points at an object nobody can check out, and the tests it lists ran on a tree that differs from the merged code.

Also (system_shape): Every task's evidence in docs/plans/0003_strap_skills_target_aware_ActionPlan.json (and its rendered PIP) names commit 156cbf1 / tree 2300ac6, and the plan's frozen record names b56b363. `git branch -a --contains` finds neither, and no commit tree in b794392..dd2089c matches 2300ac6. The plugins/ and tests/ content at 156cbf1 matches the head, but the evidence points at objects that a gc will remove, so the record cannot be traced through the merged history.

Also (roast): Every task's evidence cites commit `156cbf1c98...` (tree `2300ac65...`), which no branch contains. `frozen.commit` `b56b3636...` is not an ancestor of the head either. The branch history was rewritten into eight commits. After the merge and a gc, the plan's verification references point at objects that no longer exist, so the evidence cannot be re-checked from the merged history.
fix: Re-record each item against a commit in the branch (for example `plan.py record 0003 TASK-n --sha dd2089c`, or the feature commit that carries each task), then render the PIP again.
If re-recording a COMPLETE item is refused, keep 156cbf1 reachable (a pushed tag or ref) and add one line to the plan saying the evidence commit is the pre-split collector commit.
Re-record the items against the PR commit that carries the same code (for example c3fcb5f, or the head) with plan.py record, then re-render the PIP.
Or add a note to the plan that 156cbf1 is the collector commit the PR commits were split from.
Re-record each task against a reachable commit (for example `plan.py record 0003 TASK-n --sha c3fcb5f` or the head), then render the PIP again.
Or keep the SHAs and add a note to the plan naming the reachable commit whose tree matches, so a reader can map the evidence.

minor.name: strap-skills spec parts do not cover the new project templates or the new contract test
minor.summary: docs/plans/strap/strap-skills/SkillSpec.json lists SKILL.md, the four harness templates as reference parts and tests/skills/test_strap_skills_skill_contract.py. This PR adds five deliverables of the same skill folder (templates/project/{skill_md,models,api,contract_test,api_section}.tmpl) and a second contract test (tests/skills/test_strap_skills_project_profile_contract.py), none of which are parts. The content hash the pending STR-11 self-gate freezes would therefore not go stale when a project template changes, which is the drift the parts list exists to catch (SKILL.md step 5: 'Add every other deliverable ... with add_part, so the content hash covers it').

minor.name: strap_lint docstring says lint_skill applies the generic rules, but it skips the CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR path check
minor.summary:
The module docstring (strap_lint.py:3-6) says lint_skill 'applies the generic rules and the harness house rules', and the next sentence defines the generic rules as frontmatter, folder name, description and ${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR} paths that exist. lint_skill (strap_lint.py:217-226) never calls _skill_dir_problems, so a harness skill naming a missing ${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}/x passes. The design spec's Lint section (2026-11-03-strap-skills-target-aware-design.md:113-115) also puts that check in the set shared by both profiles. The strap-skills SKILL.md Lint row (SKILL.md:40) and plan TASK-4 ('lint_skill output stays byte-identical') match the code, so the docstring and the design spec are the texts that drift.

Also (roast): The module docstring says `lint_skill` "applies the generic rules and the harness house rules" and defines the generic rules as including `${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}` paths that exist. `lint_skill` never calls `_skill_dir_problems`; only `lint_project_skill` does. The design (lines 113-115) also lists that check as generic for both profiles. The plan kept harness lint output byte-identical, which is the sensible choice, but the docstring did not get the memo.
fix: Reword strap_lint.py:3-6 so lint_skill applies the shared frontmatter, folder-name and description rules plus the harness house rules, and the ${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR} path check is project-only.

Or add _skill_dir_problems(plugin_dir / 'skills' / name, body) to lint_skill so the harness profile gets the generic set the design spec describes, then rerun tests/lib/test_strap_lint.py and strap.py check on the existing harness specs.

Reword the docstring: `lint_skill` applies the frontmatter, folder-name and description rules plus the harness house rules; `lint_project_skill` applies those shared rules plus the `${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}` path check.
Add `_skill_dir_problems(plugin_dir / 'skills' / name, body)` to `lint_skill` and accept the harness output change (update tests/lib/test_strap_lint.py).

minor.name: SkillSpec schema description says exactly one of plugin_dir and target is set, but the schema allows neither or both
minor.summary:
The regenerated SkillSpec.schema.json carries the model docstring ('exactly one of the two is set') as its top-level description, while both properties are nullable with default null and neither is required. A JSON document with neither field, or with both, validates against the schema, and only the pydantic _one_destination validator (strap_models.py:409-413) rejects it. An editor or any jsonschema consumer is told one rule and enforces a looser one.

Also (config): The top-level description (line 606) says exactly one of plugin_dir and target is set. The schema now requires only name and mode (713-716), and both fields are anyOf [x, null] with default null, so a JSON Schema consumer accepts a spec with neither field or with both. Only the pydantic _one_destination validator (strap_models.py:409-413) enforces the rule. The drift test's only sample spec is harness-shaped (tests/schemas/test_skillspec_schema_drift.py:60), so no test validates a target-only document against the committed schema, and none shows that the schema accepts a neither/both document the model rejects. _base_iff_edit has the same model-only precedent, so this is a documentation-fidelity gap, not a runtime break.
fix: Add a json_schema_extra to SkillSpec that emits the constraint (for example a oneOf over {plugin_dir: string, target: null} and {plugin_dir: null, target: object}), then regenerate with tools/gen_skillspec_schema.py.
Or reword the docstring so it says the exactly-one rule is checked by the model validator, not by the schema.

Encode the rule in the generated schema: add a json_schema_extra to SkillSpec's model_config with a oneOf of two branches (plugin_dir a string with target absent or null, and target an object with plugin_dir absent or null), regenerate, and add drift-test cases: a target-only spec validates, and neither/both are rejected.

Or keep the schema permissive, and reword the description to say the model enforces the exactly-one rule beyond the schema. Then add a target-shaped sample to test_dump_spec_validates_against_committed_schema so the project profile's document shape is pinned against the committed file.

minor.name: Profile.templates is dead; scaffold keeps its own template-folder truth
minor.summary:
strap_profile.py declares TEMPLATES (line 26) and a Profile.templates field (line 49) set per profile (lines 70, 81), and the module docstring claims the profile answers 'every path ... the driver asks of a spec'. No runtime code reads Profile.templates: strap_scaffold.py resolves templates from its own _TEMPLATE_DIR (line 30) and the 'project/'-prefixed _PROJECT_TEMPLATES (lines 38-43), switching on profile.kind (line 162). Only tests/lib/test_strap_profile.py:37,49 assert the field. Two sources describe the same folder layout and can drift apart. strap_profile._snake (line 33) also duplicates strap_scaffold._snake (line 91).

Also (overall): Profile.templates (strap_profile.py:49, filled at 70 and 81 from TEMPLATES at 26) is read by no production code: strap_scaffold picks templates from its own _TEMPLATE_DIR plus _PROJECT_TEMPLATES and branches on profile.kind (strap_scaffold.py:30-44, 160-163). Only tests/lib/test_strap_profile.py:37,49 assert the field. strap_profile._snake (33-34) also duplicates strap_scaffold._snake. The two template-folder definitions can drift silently, and the module docstring's claim that the profile answers 'every path ... the driver asks' does not hold for templates.

Also (system_shape): strap_profile.py defines TEMPLATES (line 26) and fills Profile.templates for both profiles (lines 49, 70, 81). Its module docstring says it answers 'every path and rewrite the driver asks of a spec'. No production code reads Profile.templates. strap_scaffold.py chooses the template set from its own _TEMPLATE_DIR, _TEMPLATES and _PROJECT_TEMPLATES (lines 33-50, 160-163), switching on profile.kind == PROJECT. strap.py:333 and :612 tell the profiles apart by profile.plugin_dir is not None instead. Only tests/lib/test_strap_profile.py:37,49 asserts the field. That leaves two sources of truth for the template folder that can drift, and the strap_scaffold literals have to stay (tools/select_tests.py anchors on them).

Also (roast): No production code reads `Profile.templates` or `strap_profile.TEMPLATES`. `strap_scaffold._template_text` keeps its own `_TEMPLATE_DIR` literal (needed as the select_tests anchor) and chooses the set by `profile.kind == PROJECT`. Only the two assertions in test_strap_profile.py touch the field, so it is a second source of truth that can drift unnoticed.
fix: Delete TEMPLATES and the Profile.templates field from strap_profile.py, and drop the two assertions in tests/lib/test_strap_profile.py; strap_scaffold stays the single owner of template names (it must spell them for tools/select_tests.py anyway).

Or make strap_scaffold._template_text join plugin_root() with profile.templates and the bare template name, keeping the spelled literals only as select_tests anchors; import _snake from one module in the other.
Delete the templates field, TEMPLATES and the two test assertions; keep strap_scaffold's literals (the select_tests anchor).
Or make _template_text read plugin_root().joinpath(*profile.templates, <basename>) and keep the spelled-out names only as the anchor literals.
Remove Profile.templates, the TEMPLATES constant and the two test assertions, and leave the template choice to strap_scaffold's literal tables.
Optionally make strap.py tell the profiles apart through profile.kind (HARNESS/PROJECT) like strap_scaffold does, so one discriminator is used everywhere.
Delete the `templates` field and the `TEMPLATES` constant from strap_profile.py and drop the two `profile.templates` assertions in tests/lib/test_strap_profile.py.

Or have `_template_text` derive the folder from `profile.templates` while keeping the `_TEMPLATE_DIR` literal in strap_scaffold only as the select_tests anchor, with an equality assert between the two.

minor.name: SkillTarget folders claim repo-relative but accept absolute paths
minor.summary: The SkillTarget description says the skills and agents folders are "repo-relative", but skills_dir and agents_dir are only minLength 1 strings. Neither the generated schema nor the model (strap_models.py:379-380) rejects an absolute or drive-letter path. target is an authored field, not driver_owned, so a hand-edited spec can set target.skills_dir to C:/elsewhere. profile_of then builds skill_folder, models, api and driver from it (strap_profile.py:73-81), and Profile.rewrite joins it onto the source tree, so the skill files land outside the project. The harness.json side forbids this: skills_dir and agents_dir use $defs/relPath with pattern ^(?![/\x5c])(?![A-Za-z]:). The spec-side copy of the same values drops that guard, and new_fields only covers the config-built path.
fix: In plugins/harness/lib/harness_lib/strap_models.py, give SkillTarget.skills_dir and agents_dir the relPath pattern (Field(min_length=1, pattern=r"^(?![/\\])(?![A-Za-z]:)")), regenerate the schema with tools/gen_skillspec_schema.py, and add a model test that an absolute skills_dir is rejected.
Or drop "repo-relative" from the SkillTarget docstring (and the regenerated schema description) if absolute targets are meant to be allowed, and state that in the strap-skills SKILL.md.

minor.name: skill_api.py summary line still says it only runs harness_lib modules
minor.summary: The module docstring's first line, 'run a stdin heredoc against the public names of one harness_lib module', is also the argparse description (skill_api.py:113). With --file the module is any file loaded by path, so the summary and --help contradict the new mode the rest of the docstring describes.

minor.name: --file API module is imported before the chdir to the project root
minor.summary: skill_api._run calls _select(args) (line 99), which runs spec.loader.exec_module (line 73) in the caller's working directory; the os.chdir(cfg.project_root) happens only around the heredoc exec (lines 104-109). The docstring (lines 7-9) justifies the chdir so 'an API that resolves its repository from the working directory writes into the project --repo names', but an API module that resolves the repository at import time (a module-level REPO = repo_root()) still binds the caller's checkout. During a green scenario run that is the developer checkout rather than the run tree, so writes land in the wrong repository. The shipped api.tmpl resolves lazily, so the generated code is unaffected today.
fix: In _run, chdir to cfg.project_root before _select(args) and keep the try/finally around both the module load and the exec, so import-time and call-time resolution agree; update the docstring to say the module is loaded and the heredoc runs from the project root.

minor.name: _agent_text docstring and role messages lag the project profile
minor.summary:
strap.py _agent_text (lines 602-612) now rewrites a project skill's agent file through profile.rewrite (line 612), but its docstring (line 603) still describes only which tree the file comes from. The absent-agent message (line 610) and _role_problems (line 340) still say 'agents/<role>.md', while a project profile reads profile.agents_dir (default .claude/agents), so the message names a folder the driver does not look in.

Also (system_shape): _role_problems now looks under profile.agents_dir (strap.py:339), which is .claude/agents for a project skill, but the message still reads 'role X has no agents/X.md' (strap.py:340). The _agent_text fallback brief says 'agents/{role}.md is absent' (strap.py:610). A project author is pointed at a folder that is not the one checked.
fix: Extend the _agent_text docstring with 'a project skill's file gets the same variable rewrite as its SKILL.md', and build both messages from profile.agents_dir, e.g. f"{profile.agents_dir}/{scenario.role}.md".
Interpolate the profile's folder: f"{sc.id}: role {sc.role} has no {agents_dir}/{sc.role}.md" with agents_dir = profile_of(spec).agents_dir, and the same in _agent_text.

minor.name: Prose-only project SKILL.md still renders API rules and steps with no API
minor.summary: For a skill with no mechanical behavior, _project_sections (strap_scaffold.py:148-157) swaps the API section for a fill-in note, and its docstring promises 'a prose-only skill names no module that does not exist'. The project skill_md.tmpl still renders, with no TODO(fill) marker, the rule 'The document changes only through the API ... `validate` refuses a file edited by hand' (skill_md.tmpl:22-23) and step 2 'Run the heredoc in the API section' (lines 32-33). A prose-only scaffold therefore states rules about an API and heredoc that do not exist, and the project lint cannot catch it.
fix: Move the API-dependent Rules bullet and step 2 into substitutions that _project_sections fills: the current text when an API part is planned, a TODO(fill) line otherwise.
Or mark both lines TODO(fill) in the template so the author has to confirm or delete them.

Or keep the seed and give the strap case a `{"strap": {"target": "harness"}}` config, so the seed is needed and the harness `new` path (find_plugin_dir) keeps its root-separation coverage. Reword the docstring to match.

minor.name: In-process API loads leave sys.path and sys.modules changed for later tests
minor.summary:
_load in test_strap_scaffold_project.py calls sys.path.insert(0, ...) and never undoes it. The rendered API's `import demo_skill_models` then stays cached in sys.modules for the rest of the session. test_skill_api_file.py has the same leak through the launcher's sys.path.append and its cached `demo_models` and `_skill_api_file_N` modules. A later test in the same process that imports a sibling module of the same name from another tmp project would silently get the stale module.

Also (overall): tests/lib/test_strap_scaffold_project.py:_load does sys.path.insert(0, <tmp scripts folder>) and the rendered API imports demo_skill_models by bare name; neither is undone, so the pytest process keeps a stale demo_skill_models bound to a deleted tmp folder. tests/scripts/test_skill_api_file.py runs launcher.main in-process, so _load_file appends each tmp folder to sys.path and leaves demo_models and _skill_api_file_<n> in sys.modules. No test fails today, but a later test that loads a module of the same bare name gets the cached one from another tmp project.

Also (roast): `_load` in test_strap_scaffold_project.py inserts the rendered tmp folder at `sys.path[0]` and leaves `demo_skill_models` cached in `sys.modules`. `test_file_binds_the_api_module_and_its_sibling` does the same through `_load_file`, appending to `sys.path` and caching `demo_models`. A later test in the same pytest process that renders or imports a module with the same name gets the stale copy from a deleted tmp folder, and it fails depending on test order.
fix: In _load, take `monkeypatch` and use `monkeypatch.syspath_prepend(str(path.parent))`, then `monkeypatch.delitem(sys.modules, "demo_skill_models", raising=False)` once the test ends (or pop it in a finalizer).
In test_skill_api_file.py, snapshot the state with `monkeypatch.setattr(sys, "path", list(sys.path))` and `monkeypatch.setattr(sys, "modules", dict(sys.modules))` inside _code.

In _load use monkeypatch.syspath_prepend(str(path.parent)) and remove demo_skill_models from sys.modules at teardown (monkeypatch.delitem(sys.modules, 'demo_skill_models', raising=False)); in test_skill_api_file add a fixture that snapshots and restores sys.path and sys.modules around each launcher.main call.

Use `monkeypatch.syspath_prepend` in `_load`, and `monkeypatch.delitem(sys.modules, name, raising=False)` for the sibling module names after each test (or a fixture that snapshots and restores `sys.path` and `sys.modules`).

minor.name: Module docstring says --file puts the API folder first on sys.path; the launcher appends it
minor.summary:
The test module docstring says `--file` loads the module 'with its folder first on sys.path'. skill_api._load_file (plugins/harness/scripts/skill_api.py:68-70) calls sys.path.append, and its own docstring says 'appended'. An earlier sys.path entry holding a same-named sibling module would shadow the skill's models, which is the opposite of what this docstring promises.

Also (overall): The module docstring says --file loads 'with its folder first on sys.path', but skill_api._load_file appends the folder (skill_api.py:68-70), and the launcher's own docstring says it is appended so a file named like a standard library module never shadows it. The test docstring describes the rejected design.

Also (system_shape): skill_api.py:_load_file (lines 60-73) appends the API folder to sys.path, and its own module docstring explains why (a file named like a stdlib module never shadows it). The docstring of tests/scripts/test_skill_api_file.py:3 says '--file loads an API module by path, with its folder first on sys.path', and the design spec's Launcher section (design.md:124-125) says the same. Plan TASK-5's action text says both 'first on sys.path' and 'appended to sys.path'. A reader who trusts the test docstring will expect a sibling module to win over an installed module of the same name, which the code does not do.

Also (roast): `_load_file` appends the folder (skill_api.py:70), and its module docstring explains why: the folder must never shadow the standard library. The test module docstring still says "with its folder first on sys.path" (test_skill_api_file.py:3), and so does the design (line 125). The plan text was updated; these two were not.
fix: Change line 3 of the docstring to 'with its folder appended to ``sys.path`` so a sibling models module imports'.
Replace 'with its folder first on ``sys.path``' with 'with its folder appended to ``sys.path``' in tests/scripts/test_skill_api_file.py:3.

Change tests/scripts/test_skill_api_file.py:3 to 'with its folder appended to sys.path'. The design spec is frozen, so note the divergence in the plan's deferred or decision record instead of editing the spec.
Change "first on ``sys.path``" to "appended to ``sys.path``" in tests/scripts/test_skill_api_file.py:3 and in design line 125.

minor.name: Role-agent check test has no negative control
minor.summary: test_check_finds_role_agents_in_agents_dir shows only that `check` passes when .claude/agents/helper.md exists. No test shows that `check` reports `role helper has no agents/helper.md` when the file is missing from agents_dir, or when it sits only in the harness location. So the docstring's claim 'role agents from agents_dir' is pinned only on the passing side.
fix: Add a test that builds with role='helper', writes no agent file (or writes it under plugins/harness/agents/), and asserts that `check` exits non-zero with 'role helper has no agents/helper.md' in its output.
